summary: Decision: when the baseline ClassifyStance path finds no cue at all and the abstract is non-empty, an 'X reduces Y' claim reads as supporting at a fixed, lower confidence if a downward finding (reduced, shorter, fewer, less, lower) has both the claim's intervention and outcome within the pairing window of one sentence that is not framing, not a question, not negated and not a 'to' purpose phrase.
reason: claimBenefitCues and supportCues only know 'reduces the risk', so abstracts reporting 'reduced the duration of Y' scored inconclusive with zero cues. The fallback never runs on harm claims or after any support, null or harm cue, so counting-path results stay as they were.
validated_outcome: 15 invented cases; cases 12-15 RED on the first version. 306 archived corpus works: 0 changes from a non-inconclusive stance, 1 inconclusive to supporting at 0.6 (vitamind). 18-study chewing-gum/ileus set: all 5 target DOIs move inconclusive to supporting, plus 1 other. Mutations: 10 of 10 caught, comment control passed.
